ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #13
====

GRADE: Grade 8
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.

   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.

5. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

6. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. Where is the library
   C. Where is the Library

7. When practising Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences, which approach is best? (1 mark)

8. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

9. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only a describing word
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only an action

----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Word Classes: Primary Auxiliaries and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 3.4.1 Intensive reading: Poetry and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 3.5.1 Paragraphing: Sequencing of Ideas and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.

2. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.

3. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.

4. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.

5. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

6. A — Where is the library?

7. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.

8. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

9. A — A person, place, thing, or idea

10. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.

11. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

12. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Word Classes: Primary Auxiliaries; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 3.4.1 Intensive reading: Poetry; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 3.5.1 Paragraphing: Sequencing of Ideas; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
